newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq unlikely to leave Intel for AMD.
newsitem.headline: Compaq unlikely to leave Intel for AMD.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said on Thursday it was unlikely to lighten its dependence on Intel Corp for computer chips, even though a former Compaq partner plans to release alternative chips this year.
Compaq expected to remain a close ally of Intel for up to ten years or more, and was helping Intel develop a new generation of chips due by the end of the decade, CEO Eckhard Pfeiffer told Reuters.
He also said Compaq was hesitant to use the K6 chip due later this year from Advanced Micro Devices Inc, a former supplier of 486 chips for Compaq.
"We placed a big bet a time ago on an alternative chip and it didn't work out," Pfeiffer said in an interview after a news conference. "We shipped some 486s but nothing came after it."
AMD has said the K6 would be cheaper and faster than Intel's fastest chip, the Pentium Pro.
Two years ago Compaq had planned to move from AMD 486s to the K5 -- AMD's answer to Intel's top-selling Penitum chip. But a one-year manufacturing hitch kept the K5 from hitting the market on time.
"We don't want to be in a stop and start mode," Pfeiffer said. "We want to bet on a safe, long-term situation."
During the news conference, Pfeiffer said Compaq expected to maintain strategice partnerships "for five or ten years with comapnies like Intel" and software giant Microsoft Inc.
He said Intel faced little "serious" potential competitors, and stood far in front of the PowerPC chip Apple Computer Inc. and IBM Corphad hoped would emerge as a second standard.
"The PowerPC no longer has a chance to be an alternative," Pfeiffer said.

He added that using non-standard chips was one of the weaknesses in Apple's business model. Apple itself develops the basic software and hardware for its Macintosh computers. PC companies like Compaq use chips developed by Intel and Windows operating systems from Microsoft.
"They have great difficulties because they have to develop all the technologies themselves. I think it will become more difficult for Apple to bring competitive technology into the market," he said.
